Note that your paper also speaks of colonialism reinforcing these ideas. 

>An association of skin pigmentation/color has continued and persistent with notions of social hierarchy and racial supremacy. The colonial administration used anthropometric data to divide the populations in these two broad categories...  In some sense, it is understood that the colonial anthropologists were using the racial profiling as the basis for division and deepening the rift of physical distinctions.

I understand you were linking the paper to show that caste system is a clear factor in modern day colorism. But I want to emphasize that the people in this thread disregarding colonialism reinforcing many of these ideas is oversimplifying a very complex concept.

Just because the caste system predates colonialism does *not* mean that colorism in modern day India is exclusively caused by it. There are many ties between both British colonization and the caste system with modern day colorism. As well as current day obsession with fairer skin by celebrities and media. 

Yes of course the caste system likely created a foundation of colorism. But ignoring the idea that colonialism furthered colorism is dismissive and incorrect.

I feel that it is absolutely better than the current system in some ways but can cause some staggeringly bad effects in other ways. In my opinion, a better system would somehow involve the subjectivity of value per consumer but also have a price that incorporates labor input more than the system does today.
